problem: Given that $F(x,y)=({y}^{2}+{e}^{x})\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\,j,$ what is the scalar curl of $F?$
worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the *scalar* curl of $F$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy))-\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}+{e}^{x}) \\  & =y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-2y \\  & =y(\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-2).\end{aligned}
$$
